organizations.name: Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin
aliases: Group for Support of Islam and Muslims
organizations.notes: al-Qaeda's official Sahel branch (sub-branch of AQIM); controls territory in northern and central Mali; forming 'attack zones' around Bamako; blockades towns until they accept Sharia; besieging Timbuktu for two months; denied signing a truce with the Islamic State

organizations.name: al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb
organizations.notes: al-Qaeda's official branch in North Africa; parent of JNIM; directed foot soldiers to fight under Ansar Dine's banner in 2012

organizations.name: al-Qaeda
organizations.notes: Helped take over northern Mali in 2012; betrayed MNLA; tried to build community alliances against the Islamic State in Menaka and lost

organizations.name: Islamic State Sahel Province
aliases: Islamic State in the Greater Sahara
organizations.notes: Controls the entire province of Menaka except Menaka town; enforcing harsh Sharia; massacres of Dawsahak communities; massive regional recruitment; leadership historically Sahrawis from a former al-Qaeda group in the Sahel

organizations.name: Islamic State
organizations.notes: New caliph Abu Hafs received mass pledges from the Sahel; weekly newsletter al-Naba publicizes Sharia in northern Mali

organizations.name: Ansar Dine
organizations.notes: 2012 al-Qaeda front group led by Iyad ag Ghali; bin Laden documents and al-Qaeda correspondence directed AQIM fighters to fight under its banner; remnants formed HCUA

organizations.name: Coordination of Azawad Movements
organizations.notes: Tuareg nationalist alliance that rebelled in 2012 and signed the 2015 peace agreement; now fighting Bamako again; JNIM approached its leadership, which rejected the overture, though foot soldiers are more receptive

organizations.name: National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad
organizations.notes: Fought alongside al-Qaeda in 2012 to take the north, then was betrayed and expelled from the cities; large, well-equipped force

organizations.name: High Council for the Unity of Azawad
organizations.notes: Formed from remnants of Ansar Dine members who disliked being an al-Qaeda front; per UN panel of experts it still maintains ties with JNIM, especially among foot soldiers

organizations.name: Wagner Group
organizations.notes: Bamako's new state patron after France's expulsion; regime protection and force multiplier; complicit in massacres such as Moura; paid ~$10M a month plus access to artisanal gold mines; presence in Gao; lost aircraft and been ambushed recently

organizations.name: Malian military junta
organizations.notes: Took power in 2020 coup; expelled France and asked the UN to leave; divide-and-conquer strategy against communities in central Mali; chose to go to war again with the Tuareg

organizations.name: MINUSMA
aliases: United Nations peacekeeping mission in Mali
organizations.notes: Withdrawing at Bamako's request; gone by end of 2023; UN panel of experts on Mali documented Tuareg-JNIM ties

organizations.name: France (Operation Barkhane)
organizations.notes: Intervened in 2013 to push al-Qaeda back; expelled from Mali; its departure removed support for Dawsahak militias and ISR sharing

organizations.name: AFRICOM
organizations.notes: Drone/ISR base 201 near Agadez and base 101 in Niamey; operations limited to force protection after the Niger coup; other drone base in Djibouti

organizations.name: Dawsahak militias
organizations.notes: Non-Tuareg ethnic militias that held the line against the Islamic State until France left; targets of IS massacres

organizations.name: al-Shabaab
organizations.notes: 'Taliban of Africa'; momentum turning back in its favor with large-scale raids and suicide bombings; AU forces due out by December 2024

organizations.name: Syrian Democratic Forces
organizations.notes: Roggio's analogy for lack of effective partners: the SDF is really the PKK, a designated FTO

organizations.name: Bridgeway Foundation
organizations.notes: Caleb Weiss is a senior analyst there on the Islamic State in Central Africa

events.description: French intervention pushed al-Qaeda back; conflict has ebbed and flowed since
Tuareg rebel groups signed a peace agreement with Bamako that was never well implemented
Tongo Tongo ambush killed four US Special Forces service members in Niger
Military coup overthrew the government in Bamako; junta has ruled since
Wagner Group deployed to Mali as Bamako's new state patron after France's departure
Fall of Afghanistan to the Taliban, the start point of the hosts' 'next state to collapse' conversation
Malian military and Wagner massacred hundreds of people after mock trials in Moura, central Mali (date not stated)
Coup in Niger (not formally called a coup by the US) curtailed US drone/ISR operations from base 201
JNIM began besieging Timbuktu ('for the past two months'), blocking food and supplies; tens of thousands fled
Hundreds of Islamic State Sahel fighters pledged allegiance to new caliph Abu Hafs in a single photo set
Islamic State took control of the entire Menaka province except Menaka town after months of advances and massacres
Tuareg militias (CMA) claimed to shoot down an Su-25 and a jet trainer and capture another aircraft; heavy fighting near Ber by Timbuktu
JNIM issued a statement denying it signed a truce with the Islamic State to fight Wagner
UN peacekeeping mission (MINUSMA) to be fully withdrawn from Mali by end of 2023 at Bamako's request
African Union forces due to leave Somalia (about 15-16,000 troops) unless extended

key_claims: Mali, not Somalia, is the next state most likely to collapse: France, the US/Europeans and the UN are gone or leaving, leaving only Wagner, which makes things worse.

JNIM (al-Qaeda) controls large parts of northern and central Mali, is forming Taliban-style attack zones around Bamako, uses blockades to force Sharia agreements and has besieged Timbuktu for two months.

The Islamic State Sahel Province now controls all of Menaka province except its capital, having massacred Dawsahak communities and out-recruited al-Qaeda across the Sahel; its leadership is historically Sahrawi and it pledged en masse to new caliph Abu Hafs.
Ansar Dine was an al-Qaeda front: AQIM fighters were directed to fight under its banner in 2012, and its leader Iyad ag Ghali now leads JNIM.
The Tuareg CMA (MNLA and HCUA) is again at war with Bamako; HCUA retains ties to JNIM, and a Tuareg-JNIM alignment against the junta is plausible but unconfirmed.
Wagner is Bamako's regime-protection force, paid ~$10M a month plus gold concessions, complicit in massacres like Moura; Prigozhin's death has not changed its conduct.
The Niger coup has reduced US drone operations from base 201 to force protection, degrading ISR over Mali.
Somalia has more time: AU troops remain until December 2024 and Turkey/US airstrikes continue, though al-Shabaab's momentum is returning.
